newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Mexican sugar exports to U.S. concerns Filipinos.
newsitem.headline: Mexican sugar exports to U.S. concerns Filipinos.

text.p: Philippine Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) chief Wilson Gamboa on Monday tried to allay fears of local sugar planters about the impact from proposed exports of Mexican sugar to the United States.
"If there will be change, we can only hope it will be on the optimistic side," SRA administrator Wilson Gamboa said in a statement.
Gamboa said he met with officials of the U.S. Department of Agriculture recently to discuss effects from the proposal to allow Mexican sugar into the United States.
Philippine sugar planters said a time table on the start of those exports has not been set and is still being discussed by the United States and Mexico.

The growers, already reeling from the effects of a sugar glut due to the over imports of sugar from neighbouring countries in the past several months, have expressed fears of a cut on the country's yearly sugar quota to the United States with the proposed entry of Mexico, Gamboa said.

The Philippines is a beneficiary of a U.S. programme of yearly sugar export allocation at premium prices. It has an allocation of 219,000 tonnes of sugar to the U.S. in the current crop year ending August 31.
The sugar planters said the United States' plans to import sugar from Mexico is part of the North American Free Trade Agreement, of which both the U.S. and Mexico are members.
But at least one sugar grower said the imports from Mexico should not be damaging to the Philippines.

"Even if Mexico is granted access to the U.S. market, I don't think it has an effect on us since even now we have a hard time supplying our sugar quota. Besides, the United States imports two million tonnes of sugar annually," an executive in one of the country's largest sugar mills told Reuters on Monday.
